explanation.text: Python can download web pages and data for you. Downloading needs the internet, so that code is for your PC. But **reading** what you downloaded works right here, with text you paste in. That is the harder part, so let us practise it.
**Build a URL.** Many web addresses carry settings after a `?`, like `search?q=python&page=2`. `urlencode` makes that part and handles spaces and special characters for you.
**Read a web page (HTML).** HTML is text with tags like `<a href="...">`. Python's `html.parser` goes through the tags one by one. You write what to do when a tag starts.
**Be a good guest.** A script can send requests much faster than a person. So:

items: Read the site's **terms of use** and its `robots.txt` file. Some sites do not allow scraping.
Prefer an official **API** (a service made for programs, usually returning JSON) when there is one.
Wait between requests (`time.sleep(1)`) and use a timeout, so you do not hammer the server.
Do not collect private personal data.
Say who you are with a `User-Agent` header.

explanation.text: `json.loads` (from the JSON lesson) is all you need for most APIs. The data comes as text, you turn it into a dictionary.

explanation.title: download a page and a JSON API
explanation.text: This needs the internet. It uses only the standard library. Replace OWNER/REPO with a real public GitHub repository, for example one of your own.
explanation.code:
import json
import time
import urllib.request

def get_text(url):
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "my-learning-script"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
        return response.read().decode("utf-8")

# A web page
html = get_text("https://example.com")
print(html[:200])

time.sleep(1)    # wait between requests

# A JSON API (public GitHub data, no password needed)
data = json.loads(get_text("https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO"))
print(data["full_name"], "has", data["stargazers_count"], "stars")

examples.title: Build a URL with settings
examples.code:
from urllib.parse import urlencode

base = "https://example.com/search"
print(base + "?" + urlencode({"q": "hello world", "page": 2}))

examples.title: Take a URL apart
examples.code:
from urllib.parse import urlparse

parts = urlparse("https://Example.com/blog/post?id=7")
print(parts.scheme)
print(parts.netloc)
print(parts.path)
print(parts.query)

quiz.question: Which is usually better than scraping a web page?
quiz.explanation: An API is made for programs, is more stable, and is the polite way to get data.

quiz.question: Why wait between requests?
options: So you do not overload the website
quiz.explanation: A script can send requests very fast. A short wait is polite and keeps you from being blocked.

quiz.question: What does `urlencode({"q": "a b"})` do with the space?
options: Turns it into a safe character, like `+`
quiz.explanation: Spaces and special characters must be encoded to be safe in a URL.
